title: Clarify that R/extendr-wrappers.R is no longer generated since the entrypoint refactor (#13)
description:
`R/extendr-wrappers.R` still opens with:

```r
# Generated by extendr: Do not edit by hand
#
# This file was created with the following call:
#   .Call("wrap__make_yaml12_wrappers", use_symbols = TRUE, package_name = "yaml12")
```

and AGENTS.md says not to hand-edit it and to regenerate with `rextendr::document(); devtools::document()` when Rust doc comments or the exported surface change.

As far as claude can tell, that workflow no longer exists since #13.

title: Better handling of `Inf` and `NaN`
description:
``` r
library(yaml12)

for (val in c(Inf, -Inf, NaN)) {
  cat(
    val, "round trips successfully:", 
    identical(val, parse_yaml(format_yaml(val))), 
    "\n"
  )
}
#> Inf round trips successfully: FALSE 
#> -Inf round trips successfully: FALSE 
#> NaN round trips successfully: FALSE
```

title: Add support for comments.
description:
It would be great if `yaml12` could be used to surgically edit a portion of a YAML document that may contain comments and/or user-meaningful whitespace.

This would require careful design to preserve a clean interface while allowing lossless round-tripping of such YAML files.

One initial idea is to materialize comments and whitespace as bona fide R objects with a `yaml_comment` class. Another option would be to attach comments and whitespace as attributes of the nearest preceding or subsequent node, but that brings its own complications.

We would also need to preserve and indicate which nodes are “non-canonical” for the emitter (e.g., flow-style collections, different variations of block-style scalars, etc.).

My preference is to avoid an explicitly stateful (R6-style) API.

Ideally, this is just an additional argument added to `read_yaml()` and `parse_yaml()`, like:

```r
read_yaml(x, preserve_all = TRUE)
```

title: `write_yaml()` to take an `append` argument
description:
Perhaps it makes sense for the default to be tied to `multi`? E.g.,

```r
write_yaml(value, path = NULL, multi = FALSE, append = multi)
```
